prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2001 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core principles: Freedom, Justice, Honesty. Government should enable people by delivering high‑quality public services, devolving power, and embedding a “green thread” across all policy.

Health:
- Cut waiting times by recruiting 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied professionals, plus 10,000 beds; £1,000 annual pay boost for lowest‑paid NHS staff.
- Prioritise prevention: free dental and eye checks, more scanning equipment, £500m for NHS dentistry, wider in‑practice testing, support complementary medicine.
- End charges for long‑term personal care; create a Pharmaceutical Agency to end the postcode lottery and lower drug costs; aim to reduce/abolish prescription charges.
- Patient Care Guarantees; stronger local accountability; independent advocates; no‑fault compensation; ban age discrimination; end mixed wards.

Education, skills and jobs:
- Primary classes to average 25; 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants (focus on Key Stage 1); paid preparation time; teacher training salary; scrap SATs at 7; reduce bureaucracy.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for poorest; raise loan repayment threshold; improve academic pay equality.
- Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 2 for adults; Level 3 for 16–24s); simpler FE funding/qualifications.
- Replace New Deal with a flexible, combined Benefits and Jobs Agency; study leave with pay for 16–24s; SME training incentives.

Law and order:
- 6,000 extra police; 2,000 part‑time retained community officers; Community Safety Force for nuisance crime; independent police complaints system.
- Focus prisons on work, skills and rehabilitation; expand effective community sentences; cut reoffending.
- Strengthen victims’ rights; keep jury trial; end most mandatory sentences; tackle hate crime.

Transport:
- Free off‑peak bus travel for pensioners/disabled; aim half‑price for under‑19s in education.
- Abolish VED for the cleanest vehicles; no real‑terms fuel duty rise next Parliament; empower congestion charging/parking levies to fund public transport.
- Sustainable Transport Authority; stronger regulation; restructure Railtrack into a public‑interest model; modernise Underground via not‑for‑profit bonds; rural transport fund.
- Double rail freight by 2010; curb road building in sensitive areas; promote cleaner vehicles.

Pensions, wages and benefits:
- Raise basic pension (+£5; more for over‑75/80); create Independent Pensions Authority; relax annuity rules; reduce means‑testing.
- Review minimum wage annually and apply full rate from age 16.
- Extra support for children on long‑term income support; replace CSA with family courts; extend Winter Fuel Payment to severely disabled; long‑term goal to zero the 10p tax band for low earners.

Business, consumers and green economy:
- Cut red tape; small business rates allowance; tougher competition law (esp. local monopolies, banking); stronger consumer protection.
- Shift taxes from “goods” to pollution: move toward a carbon tax; 10% UK renewables by 2010 (rising annually); phase out nuclear at end of life; expand energy efficiency.

Constitution and civil liberties:
- Fair votes: AV+ referendum for Westminster (ultimately STV); STV for local/European elections; elected Senate; stronger Parliament and FOI; votes at 16.
- Equality Act and Commission; repeal Section 28; stronger privacy/surveillance safeguards; humane, faster asylum system, end vouchers; more devolution and local income tax.

Communities, rural/urban:
- One‑stop regeneration grants; protect local services; brownfield‑first with VAT/business rate reform; national recycling programme; CAP/CFP reform; create a Ministry for Rural Affairs.

Europe, foreign policy and defence:
- Pro‑EU reform: constitution to define powers, greater transparency, enlargement, stronger CFSP; euro entry via referendum at a sustainable rate.
- End subsidies for arms exports; 0.7% aid target; faster debt relief; fair trade with environmental safeguards; support ICC/UN peacekeeping.
- Maintain defence spending; flexible, deployable forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; oppose US NMD.
